newsitem.title: CHINA: China tells cities to use unleaded gasoline.
newsitem.headline: China tells cities to use unleaded gasoline.

text.p: China will require eight major cities to provide unleaded gasoline in 1998 to help reduce air pollution from motor vehicles, the official China Daily newspaper reported on Thursday.
Beijing will require gasoline stations nationwide to provide unleaded gasoline by 2000, the report said, quoting Wu Dihua, deputy director of China Petrochemical Corp's development centre.
The eight cities which will use unleaded gasoline from next year are Beijing, Tianjin, Shanghai, Shenyang, Xian, Guangzhou, Shenzhen and Zhuhai, the report said.
Beijing had begun the shift to unleaded gasoline from June 1.

China produces roughly 35 million tonnes of gasoline annually and the government wants 40 percent of the total to be unleaded, Wu said. He gave no figure for the current percentage of unleaded gasoline of total production.
